source_read: PMC HTML, PMC12414628 (Cochrane Database Syst Rev 2010, CD005063.pub3), read in full in my own browser tab: the first 120,000 characters with get_page_text and the rest with javascript_tool. This covered the abstract, plain language summary, summary of findings tables 1-2, background, methods, results (including Additional tables 1-6), discussion, authors' conclusions, Data and analyses overview tables, characteristics of included and excluded studies, contributions, sources of support and declarations of interest. The forest plots, which are images only, were read on PMC's figure pages: Analyses 1.1, 2.1, 2.2 and 2.13. No supplement exists.

claims.overstatement: Mostly faithful. Points: (1) The parenthesis '(most of them of chlordiazepoxide; ...)' does not fit this review's placebo-controlled evidence. Of the three seizure trials, Kaim 1969 used chlordiazepoxide, Naranjo 1983 lorazepam and Sellers 1983 diazepam. Of the review's 11 placebo-controlled trials, 5 used chlordiazepoxide and 5 diazepam. Only by participants does chlordiazepoxide dominate (Kaim 1969: 233 of 324, 72%). The wording may come from Mayo-Smith (1997), but it should not be read as describing this review. (2) The sentence ending 'adverse events tended to be more frequent with benzodiazepines (1.31, 0.99 to 1.72)' follows the anticonvulsant results, so it reads as if the 1.31 were against anticonvulsants. It is against all other drugs pooled (18 trials). Against anticonvulsants the review gives 1.50 (0.83 to 2.70), graded high. (3) This review does not say the outcome definitions predate DSM-IV; it includes trials to 2009, some using DSM-IV-TR. For exclusions it says people with severe hepatic, heart or lung disease were often (not usually) excluded; the claim says 'usually' and adds kidney disease and other drug dependence. Several included trials do list renal disease or other drug dependence as exclusions. (4) 'Reduced' is acceptable for randomized evidence that the review grades moderate, given that the claim states the small number of events and the dominance of one trial.
claims.note: Every number in the statement and magnitude that comes from this review matches the text, the summary of findings tables or the forest plots. Against placebo, seizures: 1/149 vs 14/175 (I² 0%, from the Analysis 1.1 plot), RR 0.16 (0.04-0.69), 3 trials, 324, moderate; illustrative 80 vs 13 per 1000 (3-55). Recomputed: 14/175 = 8.0% is the assumed risk; 80 x 0.16 = 12.8, so 13 per 1000; 1/149 = 0.7%. 'About 1 against 8 in 100' holds. Against other drugs: seizures 5/442 vs 37/786 (Analysis 2.1 plot), RR 0.52 (0.21-1.31), 12 trials, 1228; against anticonvulsants 1.70 (0.39-7.37), 7 trials, 523 (4 vs 2 events). Delirium 0.65 (0.21-1.98), 8 trials, 893, I² 52% (14/321 vs 43/572); against anticonvulsants 1.90 (0.43-8.38), 5 trials, 342 (13/159 vs 7/183, I² 42%). Adverse events 1.31 (0.99-1.72), 18 trials, 919, low. Deaths (Analysis 2.13 plot): 32 trials, deaths in 4 (Golbert 1967 0/12 vs 2/37; Kaim 1969 0/103 vs 2/304; Kaim 1972 0/46 vs 1/142; Lenzenhuber 1999 2/21 vs 0/21). My sums are 2 vs 5, the same as the editors'. The review text gives 4 of 21 studies and lists Malcolm 2002 twice (the plot has Malcolm 1989 and Malcolm 2002), so the claim's 4 of 32 follows the plot correctly. 'One trial from 1969 supplies most of the events' is confirmed: Kaim 1969 gives 10 of the 15 events, 233 of the 324 participants and 51.7% of the weight, though the plot mislabels it 'Kaim 1972' (its group sizes, 103 and 130, are Kaim 1969's in the characteristics table). I cannot check from this review alone which trials it shares with Mayo-Smith. The comparator mix matches 'anticonvulsants, antipsychotics, clonidine, beta-blockers and others'. But the seizure comparison against other drugs is dominated by Kaim 1969, whose comparator arms were chlorpromazine, hydroxyzine and thiamine: 27 of the 37 comparator events. The review's 'anticonvulsant' group includes barbiturates, chlormethiazole and paraldehyde with chloral hydrate. Funding: Department of Epidemiology, ASL RM/E Rome (internal) and AIFA, the Italian medicines agency (external); declarations of interest: none. This matches the claim.

anchors.locator: Abstract > Search methods; Methods > Search methods for identification of studies > Electronic searches
anchors.extracted: Cochrane Drugs and Alcohol Group register to December 2009; PubMed 1966-December 2009; EMBASE 1988-2009; CINAHL 1982-2009; EconLIT 1969-2009; reference lists, conference proceedings, investigator contact; no language restriction.

anchors.locator: Results > Effects of interventions > Comparison 1, 1.1 Alcohol withdrawal seizures; Analysis 1.1 forest plot (PMC figure page)
anchors.extracted: 3 placebo-controlled trials (Kaim 1969, Naranjo 1983, Sellers 1983), 324 participants: seizures 1/149 on benzodiazepines vs 14/175 on placebo; RR 0.16 (0.04-0.69), random effects; heterogeneity chi² 0.27, df 2, I² 0%; Z 2.46, P = 0.014. Per trial: 1/103 vs 9/130 (weight 51.7%; plot label 'Kaim 1972'), Naranjo 0/21 vs 1/20, Sellers 0/25 vs 4/25.

anchors.locator: Summary of findings for the main comparison (benzodiazepine vs placebo), seizures row and footnote 1
anchors.extracted: Illustrative risk: 80 per 1000 with placebo vs 13 per 1000 (3-55) with benzodiazepine (medium-risk population 69 vs 11 per 1000); RR 0.16 (0.04-0.69); 324 participants, 3 studies; GRADE moderate, downgraded because allocation concealment was unclear in 2 of 3 studies.

anchors.locator: Results > Description of studies > Included studies, Additional table 1 (benzodiazepines vs placebo); Characteristics of included studies: Kaim 1969, Naranjo 1983, Sellers 1983
anchors.extracted: 11 placebo-controlled trials: chlordiazepoxide 5 (Burroughs 1985a, Kaim 1969, Kaim 1972, McLendon 1980, Sellers 1977), diazepam 5 (Adinoff 1994, Krupitsky 2007, Martin 1975, Mielke 1976, Sellers 1983), lorazepam 1 (Naranjo 1983). In the seizure analysis: Kaim 1969, 537 newly admitted men, age 55 or under, chlordiazepoxide 103 vs placebo 130 (with chlorpromazine, hydroxyzine and thiamine arms); Naranjo 1983, 41 outpatients without medical complications, lorazepam vs placebo; Sellers 1983, 50 patients, diazepam vs placebo, with phenytoin given in both arms to people with a history of withdrawal seizures.

anchors.locator: Results > Risk of bias in included studies, 1st and 2nd paragraphs; Methods > Criteria for considering studies > Types of studies; Characteristics of included studies (sequence generation rows)
anchors.extracted: The review states all 64 included studies were RCTs (its methods also admitted controlled clinical trials). Sequence generation adequate in 16, unclear in 43, inadequate in 5 (Golbert 1967, Lapierre 1983, Longo 2002, Lucht 2003, Overall 1973; Lucht and Overall allocated by order of admission or rotation). Allocation concealment adequate in 13, unclear in 47, inadequate in 4. All three placebo seizure trials have unclear sequence generation and concealment.

anchors.locator: Results > Effects of interventions > Comparison 2, 2.1 Alcohol withdrawal seizures; Analysis 2.1 forest plot; Summary of findings 2
anchors.extracted: Against any other drug: 12 trials, 1228 participants, 5/442 vs 37/786, RR 0.52 (0.21-1.31), I² 0%, GRADE moderate (illustrative 47 vs 24 per 1000). Kaim 1969 contributes 1/103 vs 27/304, its comparator arms being chlorpromazine, hydroxyzine and thiamine. Against anticonvulsants: 7 trials, 523, 4/244 vs 2/279, RR 1.70 (0.39-7.37), I² 0%, GRADE moderate.

anchors.locator: Results > Effects of interventions > Comparison 2, 2.2 Alcohol withdrawal delirium; Analysis 2.2 forest plot
anchors.extracted: Against any other drug: 8 trials, 893, 14/321 vs 43/572, RR 0.65 (0.21-1.98), tau² 1.16, chi² 14.46, df 7, P = 0.04, I² 52%. Against anticonvulsants: 5 trials, 342, 13/159 vs 7/183, RR 1.90 (0.43-8.38), I² 42%; Golbert 1967 (chlordiazepoxide 6/12 vs paraldehyde with chloral hydrate 1/12) weight 26.3%.

anchors.locator: Results > Effects of interventions > Comparison 2, 2.11 Adverse events; Summary of findings 2
anchors.extracted: At least one adverse event, benzodiazepine vs any other drug: 18 trials, 919, RR 1.31 (0.99-1.72), GRADE low (allocation concealment adequate in 6/18). Against anticonvulsants: 9 trials, 471, RR 1.50 (0.83-2.70), GRADE high.

anchors.locator: Results > Effects of interventions > Comparison 2, 2.13 Mortality; Analysis 2.13 forest plot
anchors.extracted: Text: 32 studies, 2088 participants, 'only 4/21 studies reported deaths' (Malcolm 2002 listed twice). Plot: 32 trials, deaths in 4: Golbert 1967 0/12 vs 2/37, Kaim 1969 0/103 vs 2/304, Kaim 1972 0/46 vs 1/142, Lenzenhuber 1999 2/21 vs 0/21 (benzodiazepine 2, other drugs 5).

anchors.locator: Discussion > Summary of main results, 2nd paragraph; Discussion > Quality of the evidence; Authors' conclusions > Implications for practice
anchors.extracted: Benzodiazepines clearly reduced seizures vs placebo but were not clearly superior to other drugs, except possibly for seizure control against non-anticonvulsants. Most trials were very small; randomisation methods were poorly described; allocation concealment usually unclear; follow-up often missing; settings unclear; no dose-response analysis; possible selective reporting. Harms data were sparse and fragmented.

anchors.locator: Discussion > Overall completeness and applicability of evidence
anchors.extracted: People with severe medical conditions such as hepatic, heart or lung disease were often excluded; side-effect reporting was inconsistent; mortality was extremely low. Several included trials list renal disease or other drug dependence among exclusions (characteristics tables).

anchors.locator: Sources of support (internal and external); Declarations of interest
anchors.extracted: Internal: Department of Epidemiology, ASL RM/E, Rome. External: AIFA (Italian medicines agency). Declarations of interest: none.

key_findings.correction: Note rechecked. The characteristics table has 65 entries whose participant numbers sum to 4631 (4597 without Pena-Ramos 1979). Burroughs 1985a and 1985b cite the same Alcohol and Alcoholism 1985 paper (minimal vs intense withdrawal). Pena-Ramos 1979's note says it reports the 1977 participants.
Read independently from the Analysis 1.1 image (enlarged): 1/103 vs 9/130, 0/21 vs 1/20, 0/25 vs 4/25; chi² 0.27, I² 0%, P = 0.014; 'Kaim 1972' label on Kaim 1969's data.
Analysis 1.2: Burroughs 1985a 1/10 vs 1/11, Krupitsky 2007 5/25 vs 0/25; I² 32%.
Golbert 1967 weights 24.8% and 26.3%. Its risk-of-bias entry says medication was assigned by rotation.
Analysis 2.5 Baumgartner 1991 means and SDs and Analysis 2.6 I² 56% read on the images.
Analysis 2.11: 93/426 vs 69/493 (anticonvulsants 50/211 vs 36/260, I² 42%). Analysis 2.12: 2 vs 1 events as stated.
Lenzenhuber 1999 is an intensive-care trial per its reference title (Anaesthesist 1999).
Analyses 5.2-5.5 read on the images: Saitz 3/50 vs 1/51; Spies 2003 at 48 h 5.8 (8.8) vs 11.5 (9.2), P = 0.036; deaths 2/21 vs 1/23.
Analysis 4.1: Spies 1996 15/109 vs 8/50; Dion 1968 and Sellers 1977 had no deaths.

reporting_issues.note: Baumgartner 1987 has 61 participants in the characteristics table; Analysis 2.5 has 20 + 23 = 43.
Analysis 2.12 axis: right of 1 is labelled as favouring other drugs.

Substance confirmed (values 19.8/18.8 and 2.8/3.9 read on Analysis 5.4), but 'never states' is too strong. The Results paragraph on fixed vs symptom-triggered schedules labels the 48-hour CIWA-Ar result as change from baseline, and the Discussion speaks of change from baseline for HARS. Better: the review never says for the pooled analyses whether values are end-point scores or changes, and its few statements are not consistent with the values printed (e.g. Analysis 2.5, chlordiazepoxide 8.6 vs clonidine 10.2, read as favouring clonidine). The consequence stands.
Malcolm 1989 is entered with SDs 6.8/6.1 in subgroup 2.3.1 and 9.8/9.2 in 2.3.2, giving -5.11 to 1.11 vs -6.58 to 2.58.
Counted: the list names 41 studies against the stated 42. The mortality list has 32 entries, 31 unique (Malcolm 2002 twice). Thompson 1975 is excluded as an intervention outside the criteria.
Found independently in my blind reading.

The Appendix 1 heading (CENTRAL, Cochrane Library 4, 2004), the missing EconLIT strategy and the abstract-only mention of HTA websites are confirmed. But the EMBASE combination lines do match. PMC renders Appendix 3 as a decimal list numbered 1-23: line 4 = 1 or 2 or 3, line 7 = 5 or 6, line 21 = 8/20 OR, line 22 = 4 and 7 and 21, line 23 = limit 22, each pointing to the right lines. The PubMed strategy's references also match. Drop that part.

Inclusion criteria checked for Spies 2003, Saitz 1994, Ansoms 1991, Kolin 1981, McLendon 1980, Mielke 1976 (no alcohol for at least 7 days, Zung anxiety 36 or more) and Overall 1973 (detoxified 10-14 days).

risk_of_bias.note: AMSTAR 2 critically low follows from items 11 and 15 both being no. Item 11 is a judgement call (pooling unlike comparators against the review's own stated rule), and the card gives the lenient reading (low). I accept the card's domain judgments as reasoned.

interpretation_gap.note: Substantial is fair. The abstract's 'protective benefit against withdrawal symptoms' rests on seizures alone against placebo; the abstract misdirects the severe-adverse-event trend; and the trial sizes are misreported.

missed: Subgroup construction: in Analysis 2.1.2 (seizures vs anticonvulsants), Kaim 1972 enters only its paraldehyde arm (1/55). Additional table 2 lists both paraldehyde and pentobarbital as Kaim 1972's anticonvulsant comparators, and Analysis 2.1.1 uses all 142 comparator patients (paraldehyde 55, pentobarbital 41, perphenazine 46). So the pentobarbital arm is missing from the anticonvulsant subgroup. Minor.

Classification and labels: Additional table 2 lists promazine, a phenothiazine antipsychotic, among Golbert 1967's anticonvulsant comparators; Analysis 2.2.2 actually uses the 12-person paraldehyde with chloral hydrate arm. The forest plots label Kramp's trial 'Kramp 1976' where the text and tables say Kramp 1978. Minor, like the Kaim label.
The card's attrition reading for Kaim 1969 is confirmed on the Analysis 1.3 image (14/117 vs 26/156), so the seizure analysis's 103 and 130 equal randomized minus drop-outs.
